## 3) Notable strengths / limitations by platform (for stakeholder justification)

### Microsoft Teams
- **Strengths:** Best-in-class **institutional integration** (Microsoft 365, SSO/AAD), strong **governance/admin controls**, broad collaboration beyond meetings (chat, channels, files).
- **Limitations:** **Higher complexity** for first-time users; meeting controls can feel less streamlined than Zoom for some teaching workflows.

### Google Meet
- **Strengths:** Strong **ease/reliability**, excellent fit when the institution standardizes on **Google Workspace**; solid security posture in managed domains.
- **Limitations:** Some advanced teaching/webinar controls and classroom management features can be **less extensive** than Teams/Zoom depending on licensing tier.

### Zoom
- **Strengths:** Very strong **teaching-centric features** (breakouts, waiting room, recording workflows), widely familiar UI; generally strong meeting quality.
- **Limitations:** **Integration/governance** can be strong but typically requires careful institutional configuration; privacy/security posture is highly dependent on admin settings and licensing.

### WhatsApp
- **Strengths:** Extremely high **student familiarity** and quick communication; good for lightweight group coordination.
- **Limitations:** **Not designed as an institutional teaching platform** (limited LMS/SSO integration, governance, archiving/eDiscovery, moderation); privacy concerns around **phone-number identity** and boundary-setting.

### FaceTime
- **Strengths:** High-quality 1:1/small-group calling in Apple ecosystems; strong **end-to-end encryption** posture.
- **Limitations:** **Platform lock-in (Apple-first)** and limited classroom controls/integration make it a poor fit for equitable, large-scale university delivery.

### Skype
- **Strengths:** Low cost and basic calling/chat familiarity.
- **Limitations:** Generally **legacy/deprioritized** in many orgs; weaker modern classroom feature set and less compelling institutional support roadmap than current leading platforms.
